mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be negative due to persistent higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from a 5% rate-swap forecast (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as labor market strength offsets inflationary pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month and CPIAUCSL increases by >0.3% the following month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows meeting the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as weak manufacturing demand reduces market optimism.
failure_condition: Over the next 5 days after the trigger, SPX 5-day forward returns are not negative or are positive with a p-value > 0.20.

mechanism_narrative: When residential housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1.5 million units for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is more likely to be positive due to improved confidence in the economy's structural growth prospects.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows after the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% for two consecutive months triggers a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate tighter policy and reduced equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2 percentage points in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the subsequent 60 days, SPX 60-day forward returns are not negative or are positive with a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both employment (PAYEMS) and consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) above their 12-month moving averages for one month predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as dual labor market momentum boosts equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20-day windows with the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not positive or are negative with a p-value < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95 for four consecutive months signals a supply-side soft landing, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as market participants anticipate stabilization.
failure_condition: Over the next 60 days after the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.5% while FEDFUNDS remains below 3%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as the market anticipates a shift toward accommodative policy.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows meeting the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not positive or are negative with a p-value < 0.05.
